editorial_notes: Worker-query-aligned follow-up: C and Aevix both include their execution participant-count query inside the common timer. Original AOT/JIT programs, clock, backend algorithms and oracles are reused. These 504 observations are a separate profile; do not pool them with the original parallel rows.

host_state.scope: Round boundaries only; not continuous or per-core telemetry. A nominal category does not prove stable frequency or placement.

limits: One warmup and one sample in each new process; cold JIT compilation occurs before the source kernel timer.
Whole-process wall/CPU/context-switch deltas include startup, JIT compilation where applicable and verification I/O.
State snapshots bracket global rounds, not every kernel; no observer runs during a timed child process.
No affinity/QoS/frequency/power settings are changed. Temperature/current-clock/core-placement may remain unknown.
Configured compute participants do not prove successful OS thread creation.
Every observation is retained. Timeouts or output differences abort the run and preserve logs.
Ratios compare temporally paired rounds, not simultaneous executions.
Position/permutation groups are descriptive; no causal hardware claim or family-wise significance test is made.
C/AOT use the same default arm64 target; JIT host CPU detection cannot currently be forced to match.
Cold process/JIT setup is outside the kernel timer but remains in whole-process wall time.
